prompt.content:
You write and improve short Python programs that build factories in a Factorio-like simulator. A program is run once per scene; it acts only through the `world` API.

Task: construct_smelting_line.
The scene has an iron ore patch. The character starts holding 2 burner mining drills, 2 stone furnaces and 60 coal. Build a working smelting line: a burner mining drill on ore whose output drops into a stone furnace, with both machines fuelled, so that at least 10 iron plates are machine-made during a verification window after the build phase. Some scenes have walls; walking straight into a wall wastes decisions.

Program contract:
- Exactly one top-level `def build(world):` (helper functions, nested or top-level, are fine).
- Use only `world.*` methods, `math.*` (`math` is already global; never import it), these builtins: abs all any bool dict enumerate filter float int isinstance len list map max min range reversed round set sorted sum tuple zip, and True/False/None.
- Attributes: `world.*`, `math.*`, entity fields, and ordinary list, dict, set and str methods (no `format`). No attribute may start with `_`; your own names may, but not with `__`.
- Banned: import, open, exec, eval, compile, getattr, setattr, globals, locals, vars, print, global/nonlocal, try/except/raise/assert, with, class, yield, async, match.
- At most 300 lines (and 20,000 characters).

API reference:
world (the only object a program holds):
  world.me() -> tuple[float, float]  # The character's position in tiles.
  world.tile() -> tuple[int, int]  # The tile the character stands on (floor of `me()`).
  world.inventory() -> dict[str, int]  # Every item name -> count held (exact up to 200).
  world.ore_tiles(kind: str = 'iron-ore') -> list[tuple[int, int]]  # Resource tiles within 12 tiles, sorted.
  world.blocked_tiles() -> list[tuple[int, int]]  # Tiles nothing can stand or be built on (water), sorted.
  world.entities() -> list[Entity]  # The entity table, nearest first. Rows renumber as the character moves.
  world.patch() -> tuple[float, float] | None  # The task's public target marker (the ore patch's centre), or None.
  world.decisions_left() -> int  # Decisions the program may still spend before it is stopped.
  world.last_refused() -> bool  # Whether the game refused the last action (a legal intent that failed).
  world.move(direction: str, stride: str = 'long') -> bool  # Walk N/E/S/W: "long" 30 ticks (~4.5 tiles), "step" 7 (~1), "nudge" 2 (~0.3).
  world.place(item: str, x: int, y: int, facing: str) -> bool  # Place `item` on tile (x, y); a 2x2 machine covers x..x+1, y..y+1.
  world.give(entity, item: str, amount: int) -> bool  # Move `amount` (1, 5 or 20) of `item` from the inventory into `entity`.
  world.take(entity, item: str, amount: int) -> bool  # Move `amount` (1, 5 or 20) of `item` out of `entity` into the inventory.
  world.mine(entity) -> bool  # Mine (pick up) `entity`.
  world.wait() -> bool  # Let one decision (30 ticks) pass.
  world.refusals, world.failures  # int counters: refused intents, failed actions
Entity (from world.entities()): row: int, kind: str, x: float, y: float, facing: str | None, fuel: float, contents: float, output: float, working: bool, remembered: bool
  kind is "furnace" | "mining-drill" | "container" | "wall" | "item-entity" | "other"; facing is N/E/S/W for drills, None otherwise

Game notes:
- Every action is one decision of about 30 ticks.
- The build phase has a 600-decision budget; running out ends it.
- `place` only reaches tiles within 5 tiles (Chebyshev distance) of the character's own tile, never the tile the character stands on, and never an occupied or blocked tile.
- A 2x2 machine placed at (x, y) covers tiles x..x+1, y..y+1; its centre is (x+1, y+1).
- A burner mining drill facing S drops its ore at about (cx+0.5, cy+1.3) from its centre (cx, cy); rotating the facing rotates that point about the centre.
- A furnace catches the ore if its 2x2 footprint contains the drop point.
- Both machines need fuel
